title: Market Pulse
body_html:
This post reflects my current views on the market, sectors, and internal breadth/momentum. Expect candid, data-driven analysis, peppered with personal insights drawn from years of trading experience. I aim to provide value in every edition, helping you to see the market through a clearer, more informed lens.

What You Can Expect

  • In-Depth Market Analysis: A thorough examination of market trends, key indices, and pivotal turning points.

  • Sector Spotlights: A closer look at the hottest (and not-so-hot) sectors, highlighting opportunities and risks.

  • Breadth and Momentum Insights: Understanding the underlying strength of the market through breadth indicators and momentum metrics.

  • Themes and Setups: A look at the top stocks in terms of relative strength, momentum, trend, volatility, and liquidity to spot themes, setups, and opportunities

Exclusive Features

  • Interactive Spreadsheet: Alongside each post, I’ll link a detailed spreadsheet that tracks breadth and momentum metrics. This will allow you to follow along with the data and see the trends I’m analyzing day-by-day.

  • Quick Video Commentary: To complement the metrics, I’ll also be posting a quick video commentary several days a week. This will provide a more dynamic overview of the market, offering you additional context and clarity.

Market Metrics

Market Backdrop: Mixed

The major indices continue to move in the right direction. Large-cap indices have pushed higher off their 10- and 20-day moving averages, while mid- and small-cap indices have broken above near-term consolidation ranges. All four indices remain above rising 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages, confirming constructive short- and intermediate-term trends. Price and volume behavior have also remained healthy, with no signs of heavy or clustered distribution to undermine the advance.

Market internals are constructive overall, though still lacking strong confirmation. New highs continue to outpace new lows in the average stock, but only by a modest margin, reflecting limited participation rather than broad-based momentum. One notable headwind is the continued scarcity of actionable setups—few stocks are forming tight consolidations near key moving averages. This suggests that many names are either extended from recent moves or still working through prior volatility, which can limit near-term opportunity despite the positive index-level trend.

Sector leadership remains mixed. Materials and Financial Services currently occupy the top two spots on the relative strength leaderboard. Healthcare has slipped from the top position to third—not due to technical deterioration, but rather a loss of relative performance versus these leading sectors. Industrials, Technology, and Consumer stocks continue to act constructively from a price and trend perspective, but still lag on a relative basis. Meanwhile, Defensives, Energy, Real Estate, and Utilities remain clear laggards, showing weakness both technically and in relative strength.

Overall, the backdrop remains positive but selective. Trend conditions support the long side, yet the lack of expanding breadth and limited high-quality setups argues for patience and precision rather than aggressive exposure.

Overall Trend: Positive

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Positive

  • Small Cap: Positive

Overall NH/NL Breadth: Mixed

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Positive

  • Small Cap: Negative

Overall Up/Down Momentum: Mixed

  • Large Cap: Positive

  • Mid Cap: Positive

  • Small Cap: Negative

Market Recap

Market Monitor (Click Here)

1. Trend & Market Structure

The primary trend remains constructive.

  • All four major indices are above rising 10-, 20-, and 50-day moving averages, confirming positive short- and intermediate-term structure.

  • Large caps are advancing off short-term support, while mid and small caps have resolved higher from near-term ranges.

  • Price and volume action remain orderly, with no meaningful distribution.

Tactical Guidance

  • Maintain a constructive but measured long bias.

  • Allow existing winners to work while avoiding the urge to force new exposure.

  • As long as indices hold above the 20-day MA, the benefit of the doubt remains with the bulls.

  • A failure to hold the 20-day MA—especially with volume—would warrant tightening risk.

2. Breadth & Momentum Monitoring

Internals remain supportive, but not yet convincing.

  • New highs continue to outpace new lows, though only marginally.

  • There has been no meaningful expansion in breadth or upside momentum.

  • Participation remains narrow, limiting upside follow-through in the average stock.

Tactical Guidance

  • Treat internals as neutral-to-constructive, not a green light to press.

  • Require confirmation from:

    • Expanding new highs

    • Broadening upside momentum

  • Until then, expect selective leadership rather than broad participation.

3. Sector Allocation & Focus

Leadership remains mixed and rotational.

Primary Focus (Relative Strength Leaders)

  • Materials

  • Financial Services

  • Healthcare (still strong technically despite RS slippage)

Secondary / Improving

  • Industrials

  • Technology

  • Consumer

These sectors are acting constructively but lag on a relative basis.

Avoid / Underweight

  • Defensives

  • Energy

  • Real Estate

  • Utilities

These groups continue to lag both technically and in relative strength.

Tactical Guidance

  • Concentrate exposure in the top-performing sectors.

  • Avoid spreading capital thinly across lagging or rotational groups.

4. Stock Selection & Trade Execution

Opportunity is limited by the lack of clean setups.

Preferred Setups

  • Tight consolidations near rising 10- or 20-day MAs

  • Breakouts from short-term ranges with volume

  • Stocks showing relative strength within leading sectors

Avoid

  • Extended names far from support

  • Chasing strength after multiple up days

  • Stocks lacking compression or clear structure

Execution Rules

  • Use ½ to ¾ normal position size for new entries.

  • Be patient—wait for price to come to you.

  • If setups are scarce, do nothing is an acceptable decision.

5. Risk & Position Management

Risk discipline remains essential in a selective market.

  • Exposure: Moderate (55–65%)

  • Cash: Maintain 20–30% to stay flexible

  • Stops: Below recent swing lows or the 20-day MA

  • Trim or exit positions that fail to progress within a reasonable time window.

6. Scenario Planning

Broadening Advance

  • Breadth expands

  • More stocks form tight bases

  • Upside momentum accelerates

→ Increase exposure selectively toward 70–75%.

Continued Selective Grind

  • Indices trend higher

  • Internals remain narrow

  • Setups remain scarce

→ Maintain current exposure; focus only on best opportunities.

Loss of Momentum

  • Breadth contracts

  • Indices lose the 20-day MA

→ Reduce exposure toward 40–50% and shift defensive.

Bottom Line

The market trend remains positive and supportive of the long side, but opportunity is selective rather than abundant. With breadth only marginally positive and few high-quality setups forming, patience is required. Let price and internals confirm broader participation before increasing risk. Until then, focus on leading sectors, trade smaller, and wait for cleaner opportunities to emerge.
